quotes.text: I started my first band when I was 12. We were called The Destinations. Not bad, right?
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: Then in eighth grade, we were Butterscotch Sunday. That one… less great.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: I knew right then. This was the best thing I'd ever done.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: They looked like girls, but they had this incredible energy. I couldn't take my eyes off them.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: Some older kids asked me to join because I looked like John Lennon. Not sounded—looked.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: And I said, 'Sure,' because the alternative was working in a factory.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: I was first chair in seventh grade and told the band director he was an 'incompetent drunken fool.' That was it. I was banned from the Rockford music program for life.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: I thought it was ridiculous. They wanted us to follow up Ain't That a Shame with another oldie. I said, 'Let Tiffany do that.'
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick

quotes.text: I literally recorded the vocals for Don't Be Cruel while lying face-down on a massage table. Mic through the face hole. As a joke. They kept the track.
quotes.publication: Rockford to Rock Gods: The Rise of Cheap Trick
